title: Old Gold Comedy Theater
paragraphs: Single-season sponsored anthology hosted by Harold Lloyd, compressing Hollywood comedy films into half-hour radio adaptations. The historical run contains 32 broadcasts; the frozen GRH/OTRR preservation set contains 30 distinct surviving programs, with #2 and #7 absent.
GRH documents the program through Single sponsored season (October 29, 1944 to June 10, 1945) on [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Harold Lloyd (host on 30 recordings), Carl Hoff (music director on 29 recordings), Bob Williams (announcer on 27 recordings), [[person|herbert-marshall|Herbert Marshall]] (host on 2 recordings and performer on 2 recordings), Ben Grauer (announcer on 3 recordings), Tom Drake (performer on 2 recordings), and Alan Young (performer on 1 recording).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.66865a83f6609315|KFI]] (originated at station).

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Hollywood comedy adapted for sponsored radio, Old Gold cigarette sponsorship and agency packaging, Harold Lloyd radio-host experiment, and Near-complete preservation from the Harold Lloyd estate.

Single-season sponsored anthology hosted by Harold Lloyd, compressing Hollywood comedy films into half-hour radio adaptations. The historical run contains 32 broadcasts; the frozen GRH/OTRR preservation set contains 30 distinct surviving programs, with #2 and #7 absent.

GRH documents the program through Single sponsored season (October 29, 1944 to June 10, 1945) on Blue Network.

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Harold Lloyd (host on 30 recordings), Carl Hoff (music director on 29 recordings), Bob Williams (announcer on 27 recordings), Herbert Marshall (host on 2 recordings and performer on 2 recordings), Ben Grauer (announcer on 3 recordings), Tom Drake (performer on 2 recordings), and Alan Young (performer on 1 recording).

The program is also connected in the archive to Blue Network (broadcast on network), Armed Forces Radio Service (rebroadcast by), and KFI (originated at station).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Hollywood film-to-radio adaptation, comedy and comic misunderstanding, romance, courtship and marriage, mistaken identity, deception and social performance, money, jobs and social class, and show business, performance and publicity.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Hollywood comedy adapted for sponsored radio, Old Gold cigarette sponsorship and agency packaging, Harold Lloyd radio-host experiment, and Near-complete preservation from the Harold Lloyd estate.
